verses.translation: On that{H1931} day{H3117} Yeshua{H3442} went out{H3318} of the house{H1004} and sat{H3427} on the shore{H8193} of the sea{H3220}.

one_way_hebrew: שפת הים — 'the LIP of the sea': the Hebrew idiom for the shore (Gen 22:17; Exod 14:30), the body-word שפה used of the water's edge as living Hebrew does.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ט (Perek 59) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (13:1): ביום ההוא] בעת ההיא EF.

verses.translation: And crowds{H2267} joined themselves{H2266} to him until{H5704} he needed to enter{H935} a boat{H591}, and the whole{H3605} crowd{H2267} was standing{H5975} outside{H2351}.

translation_notes: נצטרך — 'he needed': the rabbinic nitpael of צרך, everyday post-biblical Hebrew; a translator from Greek writes ἀναγκάζω-equivalents, a Hebrew author writes נצטרך.

verses.translation: And he spoke{H1696} to them many{H7227} things{H1697} in parables{H4912}, and said{H559} to them: A man{H376} goes out{H3318} of his house{H1004} in the morning{H1242} to sow{H2232} his seed{H2233}.

one_way_hebrew: משלים (H4912) — the mashal, the native Hebrew category of parable (Ezek 17:2; Prov 1:1), running as a refrain through this whole chapter (vv. 3, 10, 13, 18, 24, 31, 33, 34, 35, 36); Greek παραβολή translates it.

The Hebrew opens the parable in the storyteller's participle — איש יוצא מביתו בבוקר, 'a man goes out of his house in the morning' — with the house and the morning that Greek Matthew lacks; the sower is the Ps 126:6 farmer who 'goeth forth' bearing seed.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:3): רבים] omit EFG; בבוקר] לבקר G; את] omit F.

verses.translation: And as he sowed{H2232}, some of it fell{H5307} on the road{H1870}, and the birds{H5775} ate{H398} it.
And some of it fell{H5307} on the rock{H68}, where there was no thickness{H5672} of soil{H6083}, and when it sprouted{H6779} it dried up{H3001}, because there was not much{H7230} soil there.

one_way_hebrew: עובי (H5672) — 'thickness' (2 Chr 4:17); עפר — the dust-soil of Gen 2:7; נתייבש — the hitpael of יבש in its post-biblical form: the parable's soil-language is working Hebrew, not calqued Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:5): וממנה נפלה] וממנו נפל AEF, ממנו נפלה DG; the לפי...לרוב clause stands in the margin of ms D.

verses.translation: And some of it fell{H5307} among{H996} the thorns{H6975}, and the thorns grew over it{H1431} and choked it.

one_way_hebrew: קוצים (H6975) — the thorns of the curse (Gen 3:18, וקוץ ודרדר) and of Jer 4:3, 'sow not among thorns' (אל תזרעו אל קוצים) — the parable of the sower stands on Jeremiah's own farming command.
The majority reading ויעממוהו — 'overshadowed/dimmed it' (עמם) — is Ezek 31:8's garden-of-God verb ('the cedars could not hide it,' לא עממהו): a tree-shading word reached for by Hebrew copyists.
translation_notes: ויעמדוהו — the base as printed ('made it stand/stop'); the mss read forms of עמם ('dimmed, choked': ויעממוהו A, DG and others), and Howard renders '(grew and darkened it).' The translation follows the sense.

verses.translation: And some of it fell{H5307} in good{H2896} ground{H776} and made{H6213} fruit{H6529} and produce{H8393} — the first{H259} a hundred{H3967}, the second{H8145} sixty{H8346}, and the third{H7992} thirty{H7970}.

The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'a hundred, fifty, thirty.'

verses.translation: Whoever has ears{H241} to hear{H8085}, let him hear{H8085}.

one_way_hebrew: The same doubled שמע formula as 11:15 and 13:43 — hear-and-obey, the Shema's verb.

verses.translation: And his disciples{H8527} drew near{H7126} to him, and his disciples said{H559} to him: Why{H4100} do you speak{H1696} in parables{H4912}?

translation_notes: The base ms repeats תלמידיו in both clauses (a scribal doubling); mss ABDEFG omit the second.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: To you it is given{H5414} to know{H5234} the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}, and not to them.

one_way_hebrew: להכיר (H5234, nakar) — relational recognition again (cf. 11:27): the kingdom is given to be RECOGNIZED, known as one knows a face — where Greek has γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια ('to know the mysteries'). The Hebrew has no 'mysteries': the kingdom itself is the thing known or withheld.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:11): שמים] השמים G.

verses.translation: To whoever has{H3426}, more{H5750} will be given{H5414}; and from whoever has not{H369}, what he thinks{H2803} he has will be taken{H3947} from him.

greek_deviations: The base reads 'what he THINKS' (מה שהוא חושב) — mss ABDEFG complete it, 'what he thinks THAT HE HAS' (שיש לו) — which is Luke 8:18's wording (ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν, 'that which he seemeth to have'), not Greek Matthew's plain 'that which he hath.' Again the Hebrew Matthew stands with Luke against Greek Matthew (cf. 12:1; 24:37).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:12): ינתן] + לו ABDG; חושב] + שיש לו ABDEFG.

verses.translation: For this{H2088} I speak{H1696} in parables{H4912}: because they, seeing{H7200}, do not see{H7200}, and hearing{H8085}, do not hear{H8085}.

to complete{H1584} what was spoken by the hand of Yeshayah{H3470} the prophet{H5030}: Go{H1980} and say{H559} to this{H2088} people{H5971}: Hear{H8085} indeed, but do not know{H3045}; and see{H7200} indeed, but do not — and so on.

one_way_hebrew: The quotation of Isa 6:9 breaks off with וכו׳ — 'etc.' — the Hebrew scribal abbreviation for a text the reader knows by heart (and again at v. 15). A Hebrew author quoting Hebrew Scripture to Hebrew readers can abbreviate; a translator from Greek has a spelled-out Greek quotation in front of him and no reason to invent a Hebrew shorthand. The abbreviation is the fingerprint of a native text.

לך ואמרת לעם הזה — the Hebrew includes Isaiah's own commissioning line (Isa 6:9a, לך ואמרת לעם הזה), which Greek Matthew omits entirely: the citation is drawn from the Hebrew Bible directly, not from the Greek gospel's shorter form.
translation_notes: The base wording swaps Isaiah's verbs (MT: 'hear but understand — תבינו — not; see but know — תדעו — not'; here תדעו stands in the first clause); mss assimilate variously toward MT. Howard renders: 'hear but do not comprehend, see but do not (understand).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:14): לגמור] לקיים EF; הנביא] omit G; לעם] אל העם A; ראה] ראו AEF; ואל 2°] + תבינו ABEF, + תדעו D.

verses.translation: Make fat{H8080} the heart{H3820} of this{H2088} people{H5971}, and make its ears{H241} heavy{H3513}, and smear shut{H8173} its eyes{H5869}, lest{H6435} it see with its eyes — and so on.

one_way_hebrew: Isa 6:10 letter for letter: השמן לב העם הזה ואזניו הכבד ועיניו השע פן יראה בעיניו — the Masoretic text's own consonants, including the rare השע ('smear over,' H8173), then broken off with וכו׳. Greek Matthew quotes the verse in the LXX's softened passive form ('this people's heart has grown dull'); the Hebrew text carries God's active imperatives to the prophet, exactly as Isaiah wrote them. No back-translator recovers the MT verbatim by accident.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:15): G omits ואזניו through בעיניו; בעיניו] omit AF.

verses.translation: And happy{H835} are your eyes{H5869} that see{H7200} and your ears{H241} that hear{H8085}.

Amen{H543}, I speak{H1696} to you: many{H7227} prophets{H5030} and righteous ones{H6662} longed{H183} to see{H7200} what you see and did not see it, and to hear{H8085} what you hear and did not hear it.

one_way_hebrew: התאוו (H183, avah) — 'longed, craved': the hitpael of desire (Ps 132:13-14's chosen dwelling; Num 11:4's craving); the prophets' longing is stated in the Tanakh's own desire-verb.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:17): התאוו] ידאגו EF.

verses.translation: And you{H859}, hear{H8085} the parable{H4912} of the sower{H2232}.

The sower{H2232} is the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}, and the seed{H2233} that fell{H5307} on the road{H1870} is everyone who hears{H8085} the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} and does not understand{H995} it: the satan{H7854} comes{H935} and snatches{H2862} from his heart{H3820} all that was sown{H2232} in it. This is the seed that fell on the road.

one_way_hebrew: ויחתוף (H2862, chataph) — the base uses Job's rare snatching-verb: 'Behold, he seizeth (יחתף), who can hinder him?' (Job 9:12, the verb's only finite occurrence in Scripture); mss EFG normalize to the common ויחטוף. Greek ἁρπάζει translates either; only a Hebrew copyist-chain produces the חתף/חטף divergence.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew opens the interpretation with an identification the Greek lacks: 'THE SOWER IS THE SON OF MAN' — Greek Matthew's interpretation of the first parable never names the sower (only the second parable's sower is identified, 13:37). The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'he who sows is the preacher, and the seed is the word of YHWH.'
textual_notes: The scan reads מלבו ('from his heart'); the circulating transcription's מלכו is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (13:19): ויחתוף] ויחטוף EFG; אדם] האדם ADEF; שמים] omit G; B prefixes משל; וזהו] זהו A, זה G.

verses.translation: And that which fell{H5307} on the rock{H68} is the one who hears{H8085} the word{H1697} of El{H410} and receives it{H6901} immediately{H4118} with joy{H8057}.

one_way_hebrew: דבר האל — 'the word of El': the Hebrew interpretation names the seed as the DEVAR of God, the prophets' own term (Isa 40:8, דבר אלהינו יקום לעולם); Greek Matthew's interpretation has only 'the word' (τὸν λόγον).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:20): וקבלנו] ויקבלנו ABCDEFG; השומע] + את G; האבן] אבן G.

verses.translation: But he is without root{H8328} and in confusion{H3998}, and when a little{H4592} trouble and distress{H6869} come{H935} to them, the satan{H7854} makes it forgotten{H7911} from their heart{H3820}.

one_way_hebrew: מבוכה (H3998) — 'confusion, entanglement': Isa 22:5's word (יום מהומה ומבוסה ומבוכה) — and the same root בוך as 11:6's נבוך ('happy is he who is not perplexed in me'): the rootless hearer is precisely the perplexed one of that beatitude. Greek σκανδαλίζεται ('is offended') has no share in the wordplay.

השטן משכחו מלבם — 'the satan makes it FORGOTTEN from their heart': forgetting (שכח) is the Torah's own apostasy-word (Deut 8:11-14, 'beware lest thou FORGET YHWH'); Greek Matthew has no satan here at all — the man simply stumbles. In the Hebrew, falling away is the enemy's induced forgetting of what Deut 8 commands to remember.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:21): צער וצרה] transposed EF; ומבוכה] ומבוסה/ומכוסה in the mss (Isa 22:5's companion word מבוסה).

verses.translation: And that which fell{H5307} among the thorns{H6975} is the one who hears{H8085} the word{H1697}, and in his desire{H2532} to gather{H622} wealth{H6239} the satan{H7854} makes him forget{H7911} the word of El{H410}, and he makes{H6213} no fruit{H6529}.

one_way_hebrew: חמדה (H2532) — coveting-desire, the root of the tenth commandment (לא תחמד, Exod 20:14): the thorn-hearer's failure is named as covetousness in the Torah's own verb; Greek ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου ('deceitfulness of riches') moralizes where the Hebrew cites.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:22): האל] אלהים EF.

verses.translation: And that which fell{H5307} in the good{H2896} ground{H776} is the one who hears{H8085} the word{H1697} and understands{H995} it and makes{H6213} fruit{H6529} — that is to say, from good{H2896} deeds{H4639}. And he brings forth{H3318} from the first a hundred{H3967}, from the second{H8145} sixty{H8346}, and from the third{H7992} thirty{H7970}. The hundred — this is from purity{H2893} of the heart{H3820} and sanctity{H6944} of the body{H1610}; the sixty — this is from separation from the woman{H802}; the thirty — this is from holiness{H6944} in union, in body and in heart{H3820}.

greek_deviations: The verse carries an explanation found in no Greek witness and not in Vat. Ebr. 100: the fruit is defined as GOOD DEEDS (ממעשים טובים — the same deeds-standard as 12:37), and the hundred-sixty-thirty are graded as purity of heart and body, separation, and holiness in marital union. The grading is medieval Hebrew piety (the vocabulary — פרישות, זיווג — is technical rabbinic Hebrew), a commentary that grew inside the Hebrew transmission of the text; Howard translates it as it stands.
translation_notes: ר״ל — the ms abbreviates רצונו לומר ('that is to say'), the standard Hebrew commentary siglum; הא״ abbreviates האחד ('the first/one'). A text annotated with ר״ל is a text living among Hebrew readers.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (13:23): ר״ל omitted in ABDEFG; מקדושה] קדושה EFG; בזיווג] omit B.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when the sons{H1121} of man{H120} were sleeping{H3463}, his enemy{H8130} came{H935} and sowed{H2232} darnel over{H5921} the wheat{H2406} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, beriyagah — and went away{H1980}.

one_way_hebrew: זון — the Mishnah's own word for darnel (זונין, m. Kilayim 1:1, the law of mixed seeds — the very halakhic frame of this parable: darnel sown into wheat is a kilayim violation). Greek ζιζάνια is itself a Semitic loanword in Greek — the Greek text borrows the Hebrew term. And the text glosses it בלעז ברייא״גה (Howard: 'beriyagah,' a Romance word for darnel) — the fourth vernacular gloss so far (cf. 11:21; 12:4; 12:42): the Hebrew is the host text.
textual_notes: The scan reads בלעז; the circulating transcription's מלעז is a typo, corrected here.

one_way_hebrew: גרגיר חרדל — 'a grain of mustard': both words are the Mishnah's (חרדל, m. Kilayim 1:2; גרגיר as the single berry/grain) — the exact idiom of rabbinic measurement ('like a mustard-grain,' כחרדל). Greek κόκκῳ σινάπεως translates a Hebrew figure of speech that lived in the halakhic academies.

verses.translation: And it is smaller{H1851} than all seed-herbs{H2235}, but when it grows{H1431} it is greater than all the herbs{H6212} and becomes{H6213} a great{H1419} tree{H6086}, until the birds{H5775} of the heavens{H8064} take shelter{H680} in its branches{H6056}.

one_way_hebrew: באנפא — 'in its branches' in ARAMAIC: ענף is Daniel's own tree-vision word (Dan 4:9,11,18 — ענפוהי, the tree in whose boughs the birds of heaven dwelt), and the mustard parable is that vision in miniature (עוף השמים nesting in the branches = Dan 4:9's צפרי שמיא). The base text keeps the Aramaic form at exactly the Daniel-echo; mss ABDEF normalize to Hebrew בענפיו. Greek κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις translates Daniel's scene without the linguistic seam that points to it.
זרעונים (H2235) — Daniel's word again (Dan 1:12,16, the seed-food of the faithful); Greek λαχάνων ('garden herbs').

verses.translation: to establish{H6965} what was spoken by the mouth of the prophet{H5030}: I will open{H6605} my mouth{H6310} in a parable{H4912}; I will utter{H5042} riddles{H2420} from ancient times{H6924}.

Greek Matthew reads 'I will utter things hidden FROM THE FOUNDATION OF THE WORLD' (ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου) — a paraphrase; the Hebrew text carries the Psalm itself. A back-translator from the Greek's 'hidden things' could never recover אביעה חדות מני קדם letter-perfect.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 13 is the mashal chapter, and in the Shem Tov Hebrew the parables speak their native tongue. (1) The Isaiah citations behave like a Hebrew author's: 13:15 quotes Isa 6:10 letter-perfect from the Masoretic text (against the LXX form in Greek Matthew) and both 13:14 and 13:15 break off with the scribal וכו׳ ('etc.') — an abbreviation only a text written FOR Hebrew readers uses; 13:14 even keeps Isaiah's commissioning line ('Go and say to this people') which the Greek lacks. (2) 13:35 quotes Ps 78:2 verbatim (אביעה חדות מני קדם) where Greek paraphrases 'hidden from the foundation of the world'; ms D adds 'Isaiah' — the same wrong ascription as part of the Greek tradition. (3) 13:19 opens 'THE SOWER IS THE SON OF MAN' (no Greek witness names the first parable's sower) and uses Job 9:12's rare snatching-verb חתף; 13:21 makes apostasy the satan's induced FORGETTING (Deut 8's word) and its 'confusion' (מבוכה) echoes 11:6's נבוך — as does 13:57's נבוכים at Nazareth. (4) 13:23 carries a deeds-explanation found in no Greek witness: the fruit is 'good deeds,' graded hundred-sixty-thirty as purity, separation, and holiness in union — medieval Hebrew piety annotated into the text with the commentary siglum ר״ל. (5) 13:32 keeps the ARAMAIC באנפא ('in its branches') at the precise point where the mustard tree echoes Daniel 4's tree (birds of heaven in the boughs) — and 13:43 quotes Dan 12:3's rare יזהירו ('the righteous will SHINE'). (6) The kingdom-similes are Tanakh measures: three seahs of flour = Gen 18:6; מטמון = Prov 2:4's hid treasure; מדורת אש = Isa 30:33's Topheth-pyre; דייגים = Jer 16:16's judgment-fishers; ויבדילו = Leviticus's separation verb; באחרית הימים (vv. 40, 49) = the prophets' own phrase for the end. (7) 13:55 reads 'the son of the SMITH' (not carpenter) and counts THREE brothers (Yosef, Shimon, Yehudah) — mss supply the fourth as גאימי/יאקומו (Jaime/Giacomo), European hands conforming to the Greek. (8) 13:58: 'he was NOT WILLING to do there any sign, for the smallness of their faith' — will, not inability. (9) 13:12 ('what he thinks he has') agrees with Luke 8:18 against Greek Matthew — the third such Luke-agreement (cf. 12:1; 24:37). (10) The rabbinic frame persists: זון = the Mishnah's darnel (with vernacular gloss beriyagah), גרגיר חרדל = the Mishnah's mustard-grain, עה״ז/עה״ב, מותר-idiom, and the vernacular glosses that mark the Hebrew as host text. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 59), 24 (60), 31 (61), 36 (62), 44 (63), and 53 (64).
